concepts.label: Audit User Activity (Server)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a distinct sub-feature of security:auditing with its own Enterprise-Edition gate, its own REST surface (/settings/security/userActivity), and its own local-domain-only restriction; not the same scope as general event auditing (security:auditing), so kept separate rather than folded in, to avoid mis-attaching an EE-only, local-only gate to the whole facility

concepts.label: Full Admin / Full Administrator (Server RBAC role)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - 'Users with the Full Admin or Security Admin roles can configure Auditing.'

concepts.label: Security Admin (security_admin)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - display label 'Security Admin' is stated directly on this page ('Users with the Full Admin or Security Admin roles can configure Auditing.'), and the internal token `security_admin` is independently confirmed in this same page's trackedRoles REST example. Distinct from role:local-user-security-administrator/role:external-user-security-administrator (the narrower, domain-scoped security-admin variants) and from role:read-only-security-admin (the read-only half of this same role, minted below).

concepts.label: Read-Only Security Admin
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - display label stated directly: 'Users with the Full Admin, Security Admin, or Read-Only Security Admin roles can view the audit configuration.' Per the registry's existing role:ro-admin note, this is the security-settings half split off role:ro-admin in 8.0, and per this note is a DISTINCT id, not an alias - confirmed by this page's own wording naming it as a peer of Security Admin, not of Read-Only Admin.

concepts.label: Local User Security Administrator
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - internal token `user_admin_local` appears in this page's trackedRoles REST example; matches this already-promoted concept's internal-name basis exactly. Note: the existing promoted description says this role gates audit-service configuration 'on Capella', but this page's evidence is squarely a Couchbase Server (not Capella) REST parameter - flagging this as a possible scope note that needs correcting/broadening during reconciliation, since the role clearly also exists (and is exercised) on Server.

concepts.label: External User Security Administrator
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - internal token `user_admin_external` in the same trackedRoles list, paired with role:local-user-security-administrator (user_admin_local); no display-label sentence on this page, so labeled by direct expansion of the internal token, consistent with the display form already used in the registry's own role:ro-admin collision note ('External User Security Admin').

concepts.label: Replication Admin (replication_admin)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - `replication_admin` appears bare in trackedRoles, with no prose classification on this page beyond being in a list of roles. Thin evidence (a bare token in a comma-separated REST parameter) - flagged in notable_absence for reconciliation to verify against learn/security/roles.md's 56-role catalogue rather than trust this mint at face value.

concepts.label: Eventing Admin (eventing_admin)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted, WITH AN EXPLICIT AMBIGUITY FLAG - `eventing_admin` appears bare in trackedRoles. The registry already has a promoted role:eventing-full-admin ('Eventing Full Admin', introduced 7.0.0). It is genuinely unclear from this page alone whether `eventing_admin` is that same role under an older/alternate internal-name spelling, or a distinct role. Per the round's instruction not to force a reuse that isn't really there, minted this as a SEPARATE concept rather than silently aliasing it to role:eventing-full-admin - reconciliation should check the real roles.md catalogue to resolve this.

notable_absence.finding: The default `trackedRoles` REST example (`admin,ro_admin,security_admin,user_admin_local,user_admin_external,cluster_admin,eventing_admin,backup_admin,replication_admin,fts_admin,analytics_admin`) is the FIRST page in this batch (and, per the registry excerpt, possibly the corpus) to name `replication_admin`, `eventing_admin`, `security_admin`, `user_admin_local`, and `user_admin_external` all together as a set - but only as bare, unclassified tokens in a comma-separated REST parameter, with no per-role prose elsewhere on the page except for security_admin and its read-only sibling. Minted role:security-admin, role:read-only-security-admin, role:external-user-security-administrator, role:replication-admin, and role:eventing-admin from this evidence per round-12's bare-token guidance, but flagging all five for reconciliation cross-check against the authoritative 56-role catalogue (learn/security/roles.md) rather than treating these mints as settled.

cross_component_finding: This page independently confirms the round-25/prior-round finding that role:ro-admin's 8.0 security-settings split has (at least) two named peers - 'Security Admin' and 'Read-Only Security Admin' - both stated in the SAME sentence pair as role:full-administrator's peers for configuring vs viewing audit settings. Combined with role:local-user-security-administrator/role:external-user-security-administrator appearing in the same trackedRoles list, this page is the strongest single piece of evidence yet for the registry's already-recorded theory of one deliberate 8.0 security-hardening initiative that splits 'manage/view security settings' from 'manage/view other cluster state' across (at least) three independent role families.
cross_product_finding: The local-only restriction on Audit User Activity tracking ('Couchbase Server only tracks the activity of local users... does not record activity for users who authenticate through external systems, such as LDAP or SAML') is the first of three identical-shaped EE-gated, local-domain-only restrictions found across this batch (the others being manage-passwords.md's password administration and manage-users-and-roles.md's account locking) - see the cross_component_finding recorded on those two records for the fuller pattern.
